programme_facts.value: Archaeological fieldwork using the latest techniques.
Philological elucidation of one of the oldest writing and language systems.
Art historical recording and evaluation of the self-expression of early human civilization.
Development of a comprehensive historical perspective through the analysis of written and archaeological documents.
Research into one of the earliest religious systems that had an impact on Christianity, Judaism, and Islam.
Discovery of intercultural relations between Egypt and its neighbors in the Near East and Africa.
Reconstruction of a diverse landscape history of a cultural region shaped for thousands of years.

Integration of natural sciences as archaeometric auxiliary sciences, including: geology and petrology, geophysics, anthropology, and various biological sub-disciplines up to and including modern DNA analyses and palaeozoology.
Students must acquire a large part of the knowledge on their own, as only partial aspects of a specific field or topic can be addressed in the courses.
Students are led to independent research activities at a very early stage, for example in the preparation of presentations.
